header:
Mounts the FAT volume of the device record on the stack (volume = device +26): clears the mounted flag (+2 bit 0), reads the boot sector into a 538-byte (26 + 512) buffer -- on a partitioned device (+4 bit 7) first sector 0, checking 0x55AA at +510 and walking the partition table (+446) to entry device +5 -- parses the BPB into the volume (bytes/sector +38, sectors/cluster +32, reserved +42, FATs +58, root entries +44, total sectors +8, sectors/FAT +48, geometry +50/+52), derives the FAT, root and data starts and the cluster count +54 (> 4087 -> FAT16 mask 0xFFFF, else 0xFFF, in +36), sets +2 bit 0 and returns HL = 0 or an error (3 no memory, 22 no 0x55AA, 23 broken partition chain, 40 zero bytes/sector or sectors/cluster).
Basis: callers + body -- the open slot FileIO_DriveAFileOps[0] (SeqByteBlock_ChannelContainer) calls it when +2 bit 0 is clear, and Fat_HandleDiskIoError calls it to re-mount after a disk error.
evidence: sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6544 `bitm 0, (xwa+2)` / 6548 `calr SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper6` -- SeqByteBlock_ChannelContainer (FileIO_DriveAFileOps[0], the open slot: ui_widgets/naka_sequencer_channels.c:2821) mounts when not mounted, then 6557 `cpw (xwa+38), 512`
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:8097 `call SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper6` (also 8114, 8132, 8150) -- Fat_HandleDiskIoError, whose header already says 're-mounts the volume'
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6097 `resm 0, (xwa+2)` / 6098 `pushw 538` -- clears the mounted flag, allocates a sector buffer (26-byte header + 512)
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6119 `bitm 7, (xwa+4)` / 6137 `cp (xwa+536), 85` / 6140 `cp (xwa+537), 170` / 6143 `ldw iz, 22` -- partitioned device: 0x55AA signature at sector +510
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6153 `lda xwa, (xwa+472)` / 6195 `ldw iz, 23` -- partition table at sector +446
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6335 `lda xwa, (xwa+37)` / 6342 `ld (xwa+38), hl` / 6359 `ldw iz, 40` -- BPB from sector +11 (bytes/sector) on

sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6499 `cpw (xwa+54), 4087` / 6501 `ldw (xsp+32), 65535` / 6505 `ld (xwa+36), bc` -- FAT12/FAT16 choice; Fat_ReadEntry's header (4705-4714) reads +36 as 0xFFF = FAT12, 0xFFFF = FAT16
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6507 `setm 0, (xwa+2)` -- mounted

header:
Fat_TransferSectorsDirect(file, buffer, count, is_read): moves the whole-sector part of a file read or write straight between the caller's buffer and the disk -- maps the position (+22) to its contiguous sector run (SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper7), takes a sector-cache entry (+34; SeqStep_FileIoCheck flags 0x28 when the old one holds dirty data), points the entry's data pointer +12 at the caller's buffer, sets its sector count +16 = min(count / bytes-per-sector, run), calls block op +16 (read) or +20 (write), then restores +12 and invalidates the entry (+22 = 0). Returns HL = bytes moved; on error 0, with the status in file +6 and 0x1E53C.
Basis: callers + body -- Fat_ReadFile (is_read 1) and Fat_WriteFile (is_read 0) call it with count rounded down to whole sectors (count & ~(volume +4), +4 = bytes/sector - 1) between their partial-sector copies through the cache.
evidence: sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:7146 `pushw 1` / 7149 `ld xwa, (xwa+4)` / 7150 `cpl wa` / 7154 `and xbc, xwa` / 7160 `calr SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper9_Helper` -- Fat_ReadFile: whole sectors, read
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:7388 `pushw 0` / 7396 `and xbc, xwa` / 7402 `calr SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper9_Helper` -- Fat_WriteFile: whole sectors, write
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6468 `dec 1, wa` / 6472 `ld (xwa+4), xbc` -- the mount (SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper6) sets volume +4 = bytes/sector - 1
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6858 `cpw (xsp+28), 0` -- count 0 returns 0
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6867 `div xbc, (xwa+40)` / 6893 `calr SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper7` / 6899 `ld (0x1e53c:24), wa` -- cluster of the position, sector run, error out
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6915 `pushw 40` / 6933 `ld (xbc+12), xwa` -- the cache entry's data pointer becomes the caller's buffer
sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6939 `div xbc, (xwa+38)` -- sectors = count / bytes-per-sector, clamped to the run

sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6955 `cpw (xsp+30), 0` / 6962 `ld xwa, (xwa+16)` / 6975 `ld xwa, (xwa+20)` -- block op 4 (SeqChan_ByteBlockE, read) or 5 (SeqChan_ByteBlockF, write) of FileIO_DriveABlockOps (ui_widgets/naka_sequencer_channels.c:2827-2828)

header:
Writes an open file's directory entry back: lets the device stamp the time word +65 (block op 6; drive A's FDC_ReturnZeroLong stores 0), fetches the directory sector (+26) through the sector cache (SeqStep_FileIoCheck flags 0x1A, which include the dirty bit 1) and packs the in-memory entry at +52 (name, attribute +64, time, date, first cluster +69, size +71) into slot +51 with SeqStep_FileSectorReturn, then releases the entry's bits 3/4. HL = 0, or 10 when no cache buffer was available.
Basis: callers + body -- the close slot (SeqChan_ValidateAndDispatch, FileIO_DriveAFileOps[5]) calls it when the file is dirty (+3 bit 7), SeqChan_WritePatchData after setting the first name byte to 0xE5 (deleted), and Fat_AllocateClusters before failing with 15 (no free cluster).

On other tracks it only consumes the status byte.
